pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: src/athena/core/catalog.py:370 A page that registers again has its whole entry set replaced in one assignment, with the class worked out afresh from the new flags (catalog.py:349). No old description or class is pinned, compared or shown to the user, so a changed description or a reversible/side_effects flip (GATED->AUTO) is adopted without anyone seeing it. That is the 'pin and diff descriptions across refreshes, surface changes to the human' rule in untrusted-result-handling.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/core/catalog.py:370 A re-merge silently replaces descriptions and the derived class. routes.py:547 pins only the page origin, not the catalog content, and nothing diffs the old and new manifests.

src/athena/core/catalog.py:14 One registry: the listing is generated from it, and validate/classify both look tools up through Catalog.entries, so listed and callable cannot drift apart. The listing order is fixed (by class, then by name, :467).
src/athena/core/catalog.py:357 The enforced validator is built from the same params_schema the capability block publishes. Rejections are in-band, with a reason and a detail sentence.
src/athena/core/approvals.py:19 The consent seat: a GATED call runs only after the user resolves a single-use, expiring approval row that the model cannot address (catalog.py:171).
src/athena/core/catalog.py:489 Only the invocation path waits on a person: the call ends by filing a card and is replayed later. Building the listing (render_capabilities) is pure and never blocks.

pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/door.ts:136 The door now forwards the caller's abort signal (hooks.ts:113) but has no clock of its own. When an agent calls execute without a signal, the abort promise never resolves and the door waits on a hung handler with no limit. server-composition makes timeouts door policy, enforced uniformly, not a courtesy left to each caller.

techniques.evidence: examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/door.ts:136 Handler faults are caught in-band (door.ts:147) and results are capped (door.ts:84), but the timeout lives only on the requester (packages/athena-bridge/inject.js:122). A native browser agent that sends no signal has no bound.
examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/door.ts:35 The published maxItems is now enforced at the door (the earlier deviation is fixed). Objects are closed (types.ts:143) and extra keys are refused in-band.

examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp/zoomTools.ts:93 read_view turns the on-screen focus into explicit ids. Later calls name an id, and an unknown id is a typed refusal that lists the available ids, never a fallback.

pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/src/scenes/surface/model.ts:30 The Surface model counts apps and accounts only as enabled/connected booleans, and the Mind scene is settings (the mic grant). Searching the mind, surface and shared scene directories found no tool registration, schema, listing or invocation, so these views do not touch a tool-protocol boundary.

pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: examples/hirelane/lib/manifest.ts:63 role_id is required by read_applicants and read_shortlist, and its legal values form a closed set the manifest itself lists, yet it is published as a free string with the set written only in prose. The door cannot reject a wrong role and the model is not taught the vocabulary when it picks the tool, against 'enums over free strings wherever a closed set exists'.

techniques.evidence: examples/hirelane/lib/manifest.ts:63 The closed role set lives in prose, not as an enum. The handler does refuse unknown roles in-band (roster.ts:91), but search.ts:79 returns that refusal as an empty bounded envelope with an error key and no ok:false flag.
examples/hirelane/lib/manifest.ts:243 One manifest is the authority: every registration spreads registration(name), which is typed to the manifest and throws on an unlisted name (:265).
examples/hirelane/components/board/tools/BoardTools.tsx:15 Group and candidate ids come from read_view and search_candidates, and later calls take those explicit ids.

examples/hirelane/components/board/tools/search.ts:21 The reads are bounded, cheap, in-memory lookups over seeded data, sized by page with a showing/of count. The technique's own rule says such calls need no budget.
